column3: The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the LORD your God”; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew uses singular “for yourself”; BSB uses plural “for yourselves.”
The Hebrew has singular “the way” and says the manslayer may flee “there”; BSB has plural “roads” and explicitly says “to these cities.”
The Hebrew says he had not hated his neighbor “yesterday or the day before”; BSB expresses this as acting “without intending to harm him.”
The Hebrew names the hand, the “iron,” and the “wood”; BSB describes swinging the axe and its “blade” leaving the “handle.”
The Hebrew describes the avenger’s heart becoming hot and says the killer had not previously hated his neighbor; BSB has “in a rage” and “did not intend any harm.”
The Hebrew explicitly includes “saying” and uses singular “for yourself”; BSB omits “saying” and uses plural “for yourselves.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “your fathers”; BSB uses “them” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew uses singular “this whole commandment”; BSB has plural “all these commandments.”
The Hebrew ends with the warning image of blood being “upon you”; BSB recasts this negatively as “so that you will not be guilty of bloodshed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the avenger’s “hand”; BSB uses the verb “hand ... over.”
The Hebrew names “your eye” and “innocent blood”; BSB says “show him no pity” and expands the latter to “the guilt of shedding innocent blood.”
The Hebrew actively says the former ones marked the boundary; BSB has the passive “was set up by your ancestors,” making the ancestral relationship explicit.
The Hebrew repeats the verb for rising or standing and twice says “by the mouth” of the witnesses; BSB uses “establish” and “testimony.”
The Hebrew calls this a “witness of violence”; BSB says “a false witness.”
The Hebrew names “the two men” and says the judges will be “in those days”; BSB has “both parties” and supplies “in office.”
The Hebrew uses “behold” and repeats “falsehood” with the witness and his testimony; BSB gives an “if” clause and says the witness “is proven to be a liar.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew explicitly names “your eye” in the prohibition of pity; BSB says “You must show no pity.”
